title: Discharging the Pascal axiom: the standard-conic case

problemStatement.formal: Open question OQ-01 of brianchon-theorem-oq-01: eliminate the shared axiom conic_implies_pascal by proving Pascal's hexagon theorem in the projective ℝ³ model — six points on a symmetric conic make the three opposite-side intersections of the inscribed hexagon collinear (det(AB∩DE, BC∩EF, CD∩FA) = 0).
problemStatement.plain: Remove the one assumption that the parent Brianchon proof still relies on, by actually proving Pascal's hexagon theorem (the dual statement) instead of taking it as given.
whyMatters: The axiom conic_implies_pascal is the only assumption left in both the Brianchon and Pascal gallery entries; discharging it makes both unconditional
The parent established the conclusion is a genuine polynomial identity (ideal membership in the six conic equations), so it is provable in principle
Exercises the projective ℝ³ model's cross-product/determinant algebra toward a fully axiom-free incidence theorem

proven: pascal_std_conic: Pascal's hexagon theorem for the standard conic y² = x z, via the rational normal curve t ↦ (1,t,t²), reducing collinearity to a ring-closable polynomial identity in six parameters (axiom-free, sorry-free as written; BUILD-PENDING).
Supporting: threeVectorMatrix_det (explicit 3×3 row determinant), stdConic_symmetric, rncPoint_on_stdConic (the curve lies on the conic).
open: The general conic_implies_pascal for an arbitrary symmetric conic is not yet discharged: the PGL₃-equivalence reduction (standard conic → arbitrary nondegenerate conic) and the degenerate (rank < 3) cases remain.
The direct linear_combination / polyrith ideal-membership discharge (the parent's preferred route) is still pending an available Aristotle service.
knownResults.goal: Eliminate conic_implies_pascal, making Brianchon's theorem unconditional in the gallery.

insights: The rational normal curve t ↦ (1,t,t²) turns the Pascal ideal-membership problem into a literal polynomial identity in six scalar parameters: the cross-product algebra factors and ring closes the collinearity determinant — no nondegeneracy hypothesis and no Aristotle needed for the standard conic.

The standard-conic case is the substantive computational core of the classical Pascal proof; the remaining work is the (separate) projective-equivalence reduction, for which the sibling's det_threeVectorMatrix_mulMatrix already supplies collinearity-equivariance under a fixed matrix.
